title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #18

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the plural of the English word mango? (1 mark)
   A. mangos'
   B. mangoes
   C. mangoies
   D. mangoss

2. What is polite when you collect a song from an elder? (1 mark)
   A. Refuse to listen
   B. Interrupt while they sing
   C. Take the song without asking
   D. Greet them and thank them at the end

3. Which sentence contains only singular nouns? (1 mark)
   A. Many girls sing.
   B. The girl carries a basket.
   C. The girls carry baskets.
   D. Girls carry baskets.

4. Which sentence uses a signal word for the last step? (1 mark)
   A. First, wait.
   B. Next, wait.
   C. Then, wait.
   D. Finally, wait until the rain stops.

5. What should a reader do at a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. Pause briefly
   B. Shout
   C. Turn the page
   D. Skip a line

6. Which is a mistake in reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Practising first
   B. Reading too fast so nobody can follow
   C. Pausing at full stops
   D. Looking up at the audience

7. Why is reading fluently important? (1 mark)
   A. It hides mistakes
   B. It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
   C. It makes the book smaller
   D. It ends the lesson early

8. Which word needs a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. market
   B. river
   C. Nairobi
   D. road

9. What does a full stop show? (1 mark)
   A. A question
   B. A sudden feeling
   C. The end of a statement
   D. A list of items

10. What is the best way to check the order of your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Fold the page
   B. Read it aloud
   C. Cover it
   D. Copy it

11. What is a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. One word
   B. A page number
   C. A title
   D. A group of sentences about one main idea

12. What should you keep the same in a paragraph unless there is a reason to change? (1 mark)
   A. The pen
   B. The time of the verbs
   C. The page
   D. The paper colour

13. Why should you not translate a saying from your language word for word? (1 mark)
   A. It is against the law
   B. The meaning may be lost
   C. Words are never important
   D. It is always easy

14. What does the Kiswahili proverb Haba na haba hujaza kibaba teach? (1 mark)
   A. Big things are useless
   B. Never save
   C. Only large amounts count
   D. Small amounts added together become a lot

15. How should you collect proverbs from an elder? (1 mark)
   A. Interrupt
   B. Take it without asking
   C. Greet politely and listen to the whole proverb
   D. Refuse to listen

16. What does the proverb Look before you leap advise a writer of a story about a careless pupil? (1 mark)
   A. Think before acting
   B. Run fast
   C. Be careless
   D. Never look

17. Which value should be shown in a market skit? (1 mark)
   A. Stealing
   B. Honesty, such as giving correct change
   C. Rudeness
   D. Cheating

18. What is a conman? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher
   B. A farmer
   C. A person who tricks people to get money
   D. A shopkeeper

19. Where can the main idea often be found? (1 mark)
   A. Only in the last word
   B. Nowhere
   C. In the first sentence of a paragraph
   D. In the page number

20. What is the subject of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. The verb only
   B. Who or what the sentence is about
   C. The full stop
   D. What is said about it

21. Which word means not inside? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. outside
   C. beside
   D. between

22. In front of means (1 mark)
   A. inside it
   B. behind it
   C. before something and facing it
   D. under it

23. What should you check in a partner's story? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. Title, characters, setting, problem and ending
   C. Only the paper colour
   D. Only the pen

24. Which question helps you find ideas from a picture? (1 mark)
   A. What page is this?
   B. How heavy is the paper?
   C. Who is in the picture?
   D. Who printed it?

25. What does a picture story use? (1 mark)
   A. Only names
   B. Only maps
   C. Only numbers
   D. Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end

26. Why should you not invent interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. It is easy to invent them correctly
   B. Nobody uses them
   C. They are learned from speakers of the language
   D. Languages have no interjections

27. What is a good way to learn interjections in your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. Invent them
   B. Guess meanings
   C. Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   D. Ignore them

28. Which interjection shows praise? (1 mark)
   A. Bravo
   B. Yuck
   C. Ouch
   D. Oops

29. In the sentence Oops, it is torn, what is the interjection? (1 mark)
   A. it
   B. is
   C. torn
   D. Oops

30. How long should each line in a dialogue usually be? (1 mark)
   A. Very long speeches
   B. None
   C. Short, like real speech
   D. One page

31. What should you do after writing a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Tear it
   B. Read it aloud with a partner
   C. Hide it
   D. Never look at it

32. Which is a polite phrase to ask someone to repeat? (1 mark)
   A. Could you repeat that, please?
   B. What did you say?
   C. Say it again now
   D. Stop talking

33. Which adjective describes size? (1 mark)
   A. red
   B. tiny
   C. round
   D. soft

34. What can you use to make a poster advert? (1 mark)
   A. Only a number
   B. A blank page
   C. A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place
   D. Only a full stop

35. What should you do before buying a product that an advert says is the best in the world? (1 mark)
   A. Check it and the price
   B. Send money to a stranger
   C. Believe everything
   D. Buy it at once

36. What does the lead of a news item give? (1 mark)
   A. The main facts
   B. A poem
   C. The ending
   D. A joke

37. What should a real-life experience description include? (1 mark)
   A. Only a title
   B. Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   C. Only a number
   D. Nothing

38. Why do we read poems? (1 mark)
   A. To enjoy language and learn lessons
   B. To hide feelings
   C. To waste time
   D. To stop reading

39. What is the treasure hunt game used for? (1 mark)
   A. Learning to sing
   B. Drawing maps only
   C. Practising following instructions
   D. Sleeping

40. Why should each step contain only one action? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To use fewer words
   C. To confuse readers
   D. So it is clear and easy to follow

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Plan a story that uses the proverb Many hands make light work. Give the title, characters, problem and ending. (4 marks)

42. What is a paragraph and what is its main idea? (2 marks)

43. Mama Neema buys a box of bananas for 200 shillings and sells it for 260 shillings. Find her profit. (2 marks)

44. State three steps for building vocabulary from a text. (3 marks)

45. Write two polite phrases to interrupt. (2 marks)

46. Explain why you should not share personal details on a form without asking an adult. (3 marks)

47. Write a short telephone conversation of six lines between a pupil and a friend about homework. Use polite expressions. (5 marks)

48. Describe how you would play Simon says with your class and say what it teaches. (5 marks)

49. Write a four-sentence paragraph on washing hands. Use first, next, then and finally. (4 marks)

50. Explain what a subject and a predicate are, then write one sentence and divide it. (5 marks)

51. List three note points from a passage about a kite on a free day. (3 marks)

52. Give two sequence words. (2 marks)

53. Write a short story of five sentences that ends with the proverb A stitch in time saves nine. (5 marks)

54. Give three questions you can ask when studying a picture. (3 marks)

55. Write one instruction from the road safety dialogue. (2 marks)

56. Write the verbs in this instruction: Open your book and read page ten. (2 marks)

57. Explain what the proverb Many hands make light work means. (2 marks)

58. Write four numbered steps for crossing a road safely. (4 marks)

59. Explain what an oral narrative is. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — mangoes
   Mango takes es in the plural, mangoes.

2. D — Greet them and thank them at the end
   Good manners include greeting, listening and thanking.

3. B — The girl carries a basket.
   Girl and basket each name one thing.

4. D — Finally, wait until the rain stops.
   Finally shows the last step.

5. A — Pause briefly
   Full stops tell us to pause.

6. B — Reading too fast so nobody can follow
   Speed that is too fast loses meaning.

7. B — It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
   Fluent reading helps meaning.

8. C — Nairobi
   Names of towns begin with capital letters.

9. C — The end of a statement
   A full stop ends a statement.

10. B — Read it aloud
   Reading aloud shows if the order makes sense.

11. D — A group of sentences about one main idea
   A paragraph has one main idea.

12. B — The time of the verbs
   Keep past, present or future consistent.

13. B — The meaning may be lost
   Sayings often carry meaning beyond the words.

14. D — Small amounts added together become a lot
   The proverb means little by little fills the measure.

15. C — Greet politely and listen to the whole proverb
   Politeness and careful listening are important.

16. A — Think before acting
   It would fit a story where carelessness causes trouble.

17. B — Honesty, such as giving correct change
   Skits can show good values.

18. C — A person who tricks people to get money
   A conman deceives others.

19. C — In the first sentence of a paragraph
   First sentences often give the main idea.

20. B — Who or what the sentence is about
   The subject is the topic of the sentence.

21. B — outside
   Outside means not inside.

22. C — before something and facing it
   In front of shows the position ahead of something.

23. B — Title, characters, setting, problem and ending
   Peer review checks the elements.

24. C — Who is in the picture?
   Who, where, what and why give story ideas.

25. D — Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end
   A picture story tells events with drawings.

26. C — They are learned from speakers of the language
   Ask real speakers for correct forms.

27. C — Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   Learning from speakers is reliable.

28. A — Bravo
   Bravo praises good work.

29. D — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

30. C — Short, like real speech
   Real conversations use short turns.

31. B — Read it aloud with a partner
   Reading aloud shows if it sounds natural.

32. A — Could you repeat that, please?
   Please and could show politeness.

33. B — tiny
   Tiny describes size.

34. C — A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place
   Adverts have these parts.

35. A — Check it and the price
   Adverts try to persuade so we check.

36. A — The main facts
   The lead gives the key facts.

37. B — Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   These details make it clear.

38. A — To enjoy language and learn lessons
   Poems entertain and teach.

39. C — Practising following instructions
   Each note gives the next instruction.

40. D — So it is clear and easy to follow
   One action per step is clear.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any suitable plan, for example Title: The Clean Compound. Characters: pupils. Problem: a dirty compound. Ending: everyone helps and it is clean quickly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: A paragraph is a group of sentences about one topic. The main idea is what it is mostly about.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: 260 minus 200 equals 60 shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the working and one mark for the answer with units.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read once for meaning, underline new words, write them on flashcards with meanings, use each in a sentence (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Excuse me, may I say something? Sorry to interrupt, but could you repeat that?
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Someone could misuse the details, so a trusted adult should check that it is safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the risk, one for asking an adult, one for a clear explanation.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any six lines with greeting, name, reason, polite words, thanks and goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for greeting, one for giving names, one for the reason, one for polite words, one for thanks and goodbye.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: One pupil is the leader. The leader gives instructions. Pupils obey only when the leader says Simon says. Those who obey a wrong instruction are out. The game teaches careful listening.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the leader, one for the rule, one for what happens when a player breaks the rule, and two marks for explaining what it teaches.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, wet your hands. Next, rub soap on them. Then rinse them. Finally, dry them with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in order and sequence word.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: The subject is who or what the sentence is about and the predicate says what the subject does. Example: The girl (subject) counts the coins (predicate).
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two meanings, one for a sentence, and two marks for the correct division.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Children go to the field, fly a paper kite, string breaks, grandfather mends the kite (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each short correct note.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, finally (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five clear sentences with a beginning, problem, ending and the proverb used correctly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence up to four and one mark for using the proverb correctly.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who is there, where are they, what are they doing, why, what happens next.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look right, then left, then right again. (or Cross at a zebra crossing.)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a correct instruction and one for a complete sentence.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: open, read
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: When people share a task, the work becomes easier and faster.
   Working / marking points: One mark for sharing work and one for easier work.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: 1. Stop at the edge. 2. Look right, left and right. 3. Listen for vehicles. 4. Cross when the road is clear.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in a sensible order.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: An oral narrative is a story told aloud, passed on from person to person, that entertains and teaches.
   Working / marking points: One mark for told aloud and one mark for entertain or teach.
